messages:
alex: heads up — for ~8m PagerFwd circuit-breaker tripped and incidentbot didn't escalate. I saw 3 delayed customer pages. digging now. @ops
jamie: on it. which circuit? service or client-side? any logs?
alex: server-side cb in pagerfwd v2. metrics show error rate spike -> cb open. logs: `503 upstream_timeout` repeated. stacktrace uploaded to S3 
priya: @matt are you on-call for pagerfwd?
matt: yes, I'm oncall. pulling logs now. running `kubectl -n infra rollout restart deployment/pagerfwd` as quick mitigation.
opsbot: automation: incidentbot did not escalate because `pagerfwd` healthcheck returned 503 and was excluded by filter rule `suppress_on_503=true`.
jamie: that's the suppressor filter again. we added it for noisy 503s but it shouldn't stop pages entirely.
alex: agreed. matt ? did restart help?
matt: restart done. pods cycling, new pods passing readiness. pagerfwd errors down to near-zero. manual pages sent to oncall during window. customers notified via status page.
incidentbot: manual paging performed: 3 pages delivered at 1729999150 — escalation didn't auto-trigger.
priya: root cause hypothesis: aggressive circuit-breaker threshold + suppressor rule combo. mitigation: revert suppressor until cb tuning complete.
jamie: can we flip suppressor to `allow_on_critical=true`? Or add a fallback route to `sms-relay-v2`.
alex: temporary config change pushed: `suppress_on_503=false` and added fallback route. monitoring alerts to validate.
matt: watching metrics, looks stable. will follow up with postmortem and action items. tagging eng-oncall and product. :white_check_mark:
alex: thanks — we'll schedule a retro. key action: CB thresholds, suppressor rules audit, incidentbot test that simulates cb-open scenario.
priya: i'll open the postmortem ticket and assign owners.
jamie: also add an automated smoke test that forces a 5s upstream latency to validate that incidentbot still pages. low-effort test.
matt: noted. closing thread once postmortem ticket is up. :thumbsup:
